title: Give the PIM Manager a custom host name
purpose: Gives the PIM Manager a custom host name (for example pim-manager.<your domain>) next to its generated Container Apps address: it adds and binds the name with a certificate, writes or prints the DNS records, and adds the name to the Manager's known host names and its sign-in reply URLs.
whenToRun: After the installation, when people should reach the Manager on a name in your own domain. A public environment takes a public subdomain you own and a free managed certificate (create the printed CNAME and TXT records first, then re-run with -PublicDnsReady); a private environment needs your own certificate (Key Vault or PFX) and gets a private DNS record. It is part of the PIM Manager release package, not a separate download: run it from the package folder that Install-Invardia (or the guided install) downloaded and verified (.\tools\setup\Set-PimManagerCustomHost.ps1).

runAs.name: Contributor
runAs.why: Adds the host name and the certificate to the Manager container app and its environment, and sets PIM_MANAGER_HOSTNAMES (a new revision).

runAs.name: Private DNS Zone Contributor
runAs.scope: -PrivateDnsResourceGroup (default: the PIM resource group); only for a private environment with -Dns Auto / PrivateDnsZone
runAs.why: Creates the private DNS zone, the A record and the virtual network links.

runAs.name: Network Contributor
runAs.scope: each virtual network in -LinkVnetIds (only when links are created)
runAs.why: Linking a private DNS zone to a virtual network needs join rights on that network.

runAs.name: Key Vault Secrets User
runAs.scope: the Key Vault named by -KeyVaultName (only with a Key Vault certificate)
runAs.why: Reads the certificate (its secret half is the PFX) straight into the upload; it is never written to disk.

runAs.name: Application Administrator (or owner of the Manager's sign-in app registration)
runAs.scope: the Manager's Easy Auth app registration (skipped with -SkipEasyAuth)
runAs.why: Adds https://<name>/.auth/login/aad/callback to its reply URLs.

runAs.name: DNS administrator on the AD DNS server (only with -Dns AdDns)
runAs.why: Writes the A record on an Active Directory DNS server instead of a private DNS zone.

changes.object: custom domain <name> (hostname add), then bound to its certificate (SNI)
changes.scope: the Manager app only; the other names and the app's secrets are kept
changes.why: The point of the script: the Manager answers on the new name.
changes.undo: Remove the custom domain from the Manager app (Azure portal > Container App > Custom domains).

changes.object: a managed certificate (public environment) or an uploaded certificate from Key Vault / PFX (private environment), named after the host name
changes.why: The name needs a certificate; a private environment cannot validate a free managed one.
changes.undo: Delete the certificate from the environment after removing the custom domain.

changes.object: the zone named after the rest of the host name, the A record <label> -> the environment's static IP, and a link to each -LinkVnetIds network (only those missing)
changes.why: So clients in those networks resolve the name. The record is read before it is written.
changes.undo: Delete the A record (and the zone and links if nothing else uses them).

changes.object: A record <name> -> the environment's static IP
changes.why: For networks that resolve through Active Directory DNS.
changes.undo: Delete the A record on the DNS server.

changes.object: PIM_MANAGER_HOSTNAMES (the name appended once) -- a new revision
changes.why: Mail links and the Manager use the custom name.

changes.object: the Manager's sign-in app registration: reply URL https://<name>/.auth/login/aad/callback
changes.why: Sign-in on the new name returns to the Manager.
changes.undo: Remove the reply URL from the app registration.

parameters.name: TenantId
parameters.help: The tenant id. The REST session is pinned to it; a session of any other tenant is refused.

parameters.name: HostName
parameters.help: The custom name, at least three labels (name.domain.tld). A public environment refuses private top-level names (.local, .corp, .lan, ...).

parameters.name: KeyVaultName
parameters.help: The Key Vault holding your certificate (with -KeyVaultCertName).

parameters.name: KeyVaultCertName
parameters.help: The certificate's name in that Key Vault.

parameters.name: PfxPath
parameters.help: Your certificate as a PFX file, instead of Key Vault.

parameters.name: Dns
parameters.help: Auto (private environment: private DNS zone; public: print the public records), PrivateDnsZone, AdDns or None.

parameters.name: PrivateDnsResourceGroup
parameters.help: Where the private DNS zone lives (for example the hub's DNS resource group).

parameters.name: LinkVnetIds
parameters.help: Resource ids of the virtual networks whose clients must resolve the name (the zone is linked to each).

parameters.name: AdDnsServer
parameters.help: The AD DNS server for -Dns AdDns.

parameters.name: PublicDnsReady
parameters.help: Public environment: the printed CNAME and TXT records exist, so the name can be validated and bound.

parameters.name: SkipEasyAuth
parameters.help: Do not add the reply URL to the sign-in app registration.

readsOnly: the Manager container app and its Container Apps environment (internal or external, static IP, default domain, verification id)
the existing private DNS record and links (before writing them)
the Manager's Easy Auth configuration and its app registration's reply URLs
network: the AD DNS server (only with -Dns AdDns)
whatIf: Reads the Manager app and its environment, prints the plan (certificate type, DNS mode and every DNS record), then 'What if: Performing the operation "custom host name <name>" on target "ca-pim-manager"' and 'preview only -- nothing was changed'. Nothing is written.
undo: Remove the custom domain from the Manager app, delete its certificate from the environment, delete the DNS record, remove the name from PIM_MANAGER_HOSTNAMES and the reply URL from the sign-in app registration.
